speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; can you tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if they are painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pemphigus Vulgaris. The patient's age, recent initiation of captopril (a known trigger), and the classic presentation of painful oral ulcers preceded by blisters on the forearm are highly characteristic of this autoimmune condition. The pain during eating and sexual intercourse confirms the involvement of mucosal surfaces.

Given the clinical picture, I need to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Direct Immunofluorescence (DIF) of the oral lesion. REQUEST TEST: Tzanck smear. REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide high-resolution images of the forearm blisters and oral ulcers for visual confirmation.
